objective: Identify the later Daniel title holders and test the unproved William-428 parent link from named kin or an actual title succession.

questions.question: What tract and prior deed underlie the 5 January 1736/7 assignment to Daniel, and does the original identify senior, junior, wife or kin?
Does the 1768 Tulls Creek boundary preserve an old proprietor’s name or identify a later Daniel, and what recorded chain connects it?

research_state.last_test: Read the public Book 3 p.45 assignment and Book 2 pp.98–99 boundary extracts; compared existing original1692/1714 title conclusions. No father or lifetime identity clause obtained. Books1/2/3 and LetterBook1 are partial published extracts, not a complete original-register search. OCCGS OCR is a lead; requested PDF page image unavailable, not visually verified.
research_state.next_test: Read original Book3 p.45 with its underlying instrument/endorsement and compare any actual tract recital with the separate Richford, Miller, Slade and New Entry titles. Then trace only the identified tract forward for named heirs or a William connection.
research_state.resume_when: An original assignment/underlying deed, forward title recital, probate/distribution or other identifying kin clause is available. Do not repeat the completed1692/1714 originals or count the 1768 boundary as proof of life.

findings.summary: Deed Book 3, p.45: Luke and Margaret White assign their interest in the within deed to Daniel Glasgoe; Lewis Jenkins and John Martyn witness. The court extract says Luke White acknowledged the assignment. The extract supplies no tract acreage or boundaries, named Glasgow relative, wife, or Senior/Junior suffix. Its reference to a within deed must be resolved from the original context, not assigned to the preceding online entry. The dual-year January date is retained. Comparison accounts and the record-defined 1714 junior remain unresolved; no life dates or parent claim are changed.

Deed Book 2, pp.98–99: Willis Lufman conveys two tracts to Neil Snodgrass and Richard Templeman; the Tulls Creek plantation bounds on Daniel Glasgow and a Williams line, with a reference to a William Williams survey in 1704. Parts of the abstract are torn or uncertain, including acreage and witness names. A boundary can preserve a former owner’s name: this does not prove Daniel alive in 1768 or connect the tract to Richford Swamp, the 1714 Miller parcel, the 1729 Slade parcel or William Glasgow’s New Entry. No parent or succession clause is exposed.
